verdict.rationale: Jules is a hosted cloud agent: tasks run in a vendor-provided virtual machine that clones the repo, installs dependencies, and edits files. A hands-on user confirms it runs in cloud VMs rather than locally, and an API lets developers drive sessions programmatically without running their own agent backend. Missing for 10: explicit first-party wording that the infrastructure is fully managed with no self-hosting, and clear documentation of VM provisioning and concurrency/scaling limits (the usage-limits evidence is fragmentary).

support.subject: As a developer, I can use a managed cloud offering to run agents without operating my own backend infrastructure

citations.quote: Jules runs in a virtual machine where it clones your code, installs dependencies, and modifies files.
Jules runs in cloud-based VMs instead of on my local machine
You can use the API to create custom workflows, automate tasks like bug fixing and code reviews
